s: God is merciful Merciful One
q: O Merciful One, by Thy name shall 1 cross over aim ever a sacrifice unto Thee.

s: God is beloved Beloved (to the speaker)
q: How shall I, O Beloved, abide without Thee?

s: God is true cherisher True Cherisher
q: The poet Nanak thus speaketh; O True Cherisher, If Thou give nothing to any one, what pledge can he give Thee?

s: man is a servant (when performing service)
q: He who performeth service is a servant of Him Who pervadeth the water, the dry land, the nether regions, and the firmament.

s: man desires more enjoyment (while engaged in pleasures)
q: Man though ever and ever engaged in pleasures, ever and ever desireth more enjoyment.

s: man forgets God (while pursuing pleasure)
q: He thinketh not of the Creator, so misery attacheth to him again and again.

s: man is summoned Death (when accounts are not adjusted)
q: They whose accounts are not adjusted shall be summoned; the executioner shall smite them on their heads.

s: man is examined accounts (when called for)
q: When the account is called for it must be given; it will be examined and considered.

s: man dies dust (when making another than God his friend)
q: If he make any one else than God his friend, he shall die and be blended with the dust.

s: man is supported by God (as Creator and sustainer)
q: He who made and sustained the world giveth support to all.

s: God pervades world (including water, dry land, nether regions, and firmament)
q: He who performeth service is a servant of Him Who pervadeth the water, the dry land, the nether regions, and the firmament.

s: God is Benefactor (ever and ever)
q: Why forget Him who is ever and ever the Benefactor?

s: God dwells in heart (as the Dispenser of weal and woe)
q: How shall he in whose heart the Dispenser of weal and woe dwelleth, want for anything?

s: God grants emancipation (by a favouring glance)
q: But he shall be emancipated by a favouring glance from God and God will blend him with Himself.

s: man wanders abroad (when not dwelling at home)
q: Man dwelleth not at home, but wandereth abroad.

s: God blends with man (after emancipation)
q: But he shall be emancipated by a favouring glance from God and God will blend him with Himself.

s: God is found by God's love (in all things)
q: In all things is Thy light; from it art Thou known, but Thou art found by love.

s: Nanak teaches man (that recognizing universal fault and goodness brings salvation)
q: I am not good; there is nobody bad. The representation of Nanak is--he who thinketh so is saved.

s: Nanak is sacrificed to friends (who have heard and accepted the Name)
q: Nanak, I am a sacrifice to those who have heard and accepted it.

s: Guru gives the True Guru's instruction (as spiritual dye)
q: Serve the Guru who giveth God's dye, and apply thy heart to the True One.

s: Guru protects man (and saves those under his protection)
q: They whom the Guru protecteth are saved; their hearts are dyed with his instruction.

s: Guru removes demerits (through the Word)
q: Nanak, he who removeth his demerits by the Word, obtaineth God through his aggregate of merits.

s: divine knowledge is a means of service (to the True One)
q: Embrace such knowledge, O my soul, As may make thee a servant of the True One.

s: divine knowledge dispels mental ignorance (when it appears)
q: Where divine knowledge appeareth mental ignorance is dispelled.

s: divine knowledge reveals God's form (through spiritual sight)
q: I applied the great salve of divine knowledge to mine eyes, and saw God's form which filleth the three worlds.

s: man forsakes ambrosia (and eats poison)
q: Why doth he forsake ambrosia and eat poison?

s: the Name supports supportless (as the essential support)
q: May Nanak not forget the Name which is the support of the supportless!

s: the Name is superior to call to prayer (and other religious sounds)
q: The repetition of God's name is superior to the call of the Muazzin or the horn of the Jogi,

s: the Name is superior to horn of the Jogi (when repeated)
q: The repetition of God's name is superior to the call of the Muazzin or the horn of the Jogi,

s: the Word removes demerits (through Guru instruction)
q: Nanak, he who removeth his demerits by the Word, obtaineth God through his aggregate of merits.

s: the Word is rejected by man (when he delights not in it)
q: They who delight not in the Word and who love not God's name, 'Speak offensively with their tongues, and shall ever be disgraced

s: mammon absorbs man (when the heart is filthy and hard)
q: Never utter the Name, but like thieves become absorbed in mammon.

s: transmigration is suffered by man (when he goes astray)
q: Man beholding various phases of life is led astray, and going astray suffereth transmigration;

s: death causes pain (through separation from God)
q: On beholding Thee I have become free from desire; the pain of birth and death is at an end.

s: God's love finds God (as the means of finding Him)
q: In all things is Thy light; from it art Thou known, but Thou art found by love.

s: man is bound by entanglements (throughout the world)
q: Yet the whole world wandereth bound by its own entanglements.

s: the True Guru's instruction adjusts affairs (of the devotee)
q: His instruction hath adjusted mine affairs.

s: the True Guru's instruction dy es heart (with spiritual knowledge)
q: They whom the Guru protecteth are saved; their hearts are dyed with his instruction.

s: saints bring happiness (by meeting them)
q: When it pleased God He caused me to meet them without Mine own effort; by meeting the elect happiness is found.

s: saints brighten house (when they come there)
q: When I meet the saints my soul is happy; night and day my hearth and home look bright.

s: house receives friends (when the True One causes their meeting)
q: Friends have come to my house: The True One hath caused me to meet them.

s: house receives Spouse (when the Spouse comes home)
q: The Spouse hath come to my house, the place is adorned by Him.

s: world is sustained by God (as Creator and sustainer)
q: He who made and sustained the world giveth support to all.

s: Pandits read the Veds (as a secular occupation)
q: You, O Pandits, read the Veds and study them, But the reading of the Veds is a secular occupation.

s: Pandits are disgraced without divine knowledge (despite reading the Veds)
q: Without understanding this every one shall be disgraced, 'Nanak, the man who listeneth to the Guru's instruction shall be saved.

s: the Veds do not destroy sinful inclinations (by reading alone)
q: You say, O Pandits--'As darkness is dispelled when a lamp is lighted, 'So by reading the Veds sinful inclinations are destroyed.' I say, 'When the sun riseth, the moon is not seen.

s: man is saved by God's love (for the True One)
q: Man shall be saved by his love for the True One; the Pardoner will pardon him.

s: man is led astray by various phases of life
q: Man beholding various phases of life is led astray, and going astray suffereth transmigration;

s: man suffers transmigration (when led astray)
q: Man beholding various phases of life is led astray, and going astray suffereth transmigration;

s: man is ruined by different directions (when drawn in them)
q: Man is ruined by allowing himself to be drawn in different directions; the effects of both evil and good acts remain with him.

s: man has demerits (in himself)
q: In me are all demerits; I have not one merit

s: God fills sea (with divine presence)
q: Thou fillest sea and land, the upper and lower regions Thy light is in every heart.

s: God fills land (with divine presence)
q: Thou fillest sea and land, the upper and lower regions Thy light is in every heart.

s: God fills lower regions (with divine presence)
q: Thou fillest sea and land, the upper and lower regions Thy light is in every heart.

s: God protects men
q: Men and lower animals all seek Thy protection; all anxiety for them resteth with Thee.

s: God protects lower animals
q: Men and lower animals all seek Thy protection; all anxiety for them resteth with Thee.

s: God bears anxiety (for men and lower animals)
q: Men and lower animals all seek Thy protection; all anxiety for them resteth with Thee.

s: Nanak is a blind man
q: I know not Thy limit, O my Lord; what skill have 1, a blind man?

s: Nanak is a strange dog (among many dogs)
q: Among so many dogs I, a strange dog, bark for my belly's sake.

s: Nanak possesses Qalandar's dress (as clothing)
q: My body I have clothed with a Qalandar's dress,

s: Qalandar's dress clothes Nanak (covering his body)
q: My body I have clothed with a Qalandar's dress,

s: God is a emperor
q: Thou art an emperor;

s: Nanak has as heart temple (Nanak's heart)
q: I have turned my heart into a temple,

s: the one word dwells in Nanak (in his heart)
q: The one word dwelleth in my heart,

s: Nanak is not born again not born again (because the one word dwells in his heart)
q: The one word dwelleth in my heart, and I shall not be born again.

s: Nanak is pierced by God (in his soul, by divine compassion)
q: My soul is pierced by the Compassionate One;

s: Nanak thinks of God (exclusively)
q: I think of no one but God.

s: Nanak receives understanding (from God)
q: Give me understanding to sing Thy praises,

s: understanding belongs to God (along with Nanak's faculty of learning)
q: My faculty of learning and my understanding are all Thine;

s: Nanak sings praises (continually to God)
q: I know none but Thee, O my Lord; I ever sing Thy praises.

s: Nanak knows God (and no other)
q: I know none but Thee, O my Lord;

s: God is a Lord
q: If Thou inspire me, I will praise Thee, O Lord;

s: Nanak bears God (as his Master's name despite performing no service)
q: Even though Nanak perform no service, he will still bear his Master's name.

s: Nanak performs devotion (none)
q: Even though Nanak perform no service, he will still bear his Master's name.

s: Nanak represents what pleaseth God (as his sole representation)
q: What pleaseth Thee is good; this is Nanak's sole representation.

s: truth is abided by Nanak (according to God's will)
q: That I may abide in truth according to Thy will.

s: praises are sung by Nanak (to God)
q: If Thou inspire me, I will praise Thee, O Lord;

s: God inspires Nanak
q: If Thou inspire me, I will praise Thee, O Lord;

s: God loves all
q: All that there is cometh from Thee; Thou lovest all.

s: God is inaccessible inaccessible
q: O inaccessible, imperceptible, unseen, and boundless God, take thought for me.

s: God is imperceptible imperceptible
q: O inaccessible, imperceptible, unseen, and boundless God, take thought for me.

s: God is unseen unseen
q: O inaccessible, imperceptible, unseen, and boundless God, take thought for me.

s: God is boundless boundless
q: O inaccessible, imperceptible, unseen, and boundless God, take thought for me.

s: the Name is named after Lord of the three worlds
q: What name shall I repeat except that of the Lord of the world?

s: God has attributes and knowledge attributes and knowledge (the subject of day-and-night immersion)
q: Night and day lave yourselves in the attributes and knowledge of the True One.

s: impurity does not cling to true heart (when doubts and fears have fled)
q: When doubts and fears have fled, impurity shall not cling to the true heart.

s: world is like cord
q: Know that the world is as the cord.

s: God brings happiness (when the mind is fixed firmly on it)
q: Fix thy mind firmly on the True One and thou shalt be happy.

s: God has court God's court
q: Under the Guru's instruction God's court is seen in one's own home.

s: the True Guru's instruction enables seeing God's court (in one's own home)
q: Under the Guru's instruction God's court is seen in one's own home.

s: mammon leads to Death's gate (for those attached to mammon)
q: They who are attached to mammon shall regret it They shall go in fetters to Death's gate and suffer transmigration.

s: mammon leads to transmigration (for those attached to mammon)
q: They who are attached to mammon shall regret it They shall go in fetters to Death's gate and suffer transmigration.

s: the True Guru's instruction is required for emancipation
q: No one can be emancipated without the Guru's instruction.

s: the tenth day of the lunar month calls for repetition of the Name (as offerings and ablutions)
q: On the tenth day of the lunar month repeat the Name as your offerings and ablutions.

s: the Name is repeated on the tenth day of the lunar month (as offerings and ablutions)
q: On the tenth day of the lunar month repeat the Name as your offerings and ablutions.

s: Nanak serves God (through devotion)
q: Nanak serve Him by whose service sorrow departeth, Sins are erased, merits take their place, and peace abideth in the heart.

s: Guru provides instruction (for spiritual understanding)
q: He who hath not received the Guru's instruction, loseth his honour by his own stupidity.

s: Guru leads people (to recognize God's will)
q: When there is the Guru's instruction man recognizeth God's will.

s: Guru is sought for protection
q: But, when the Guru's protection is sought, happiness resulteth.

s: Jogis is a religious ascetic (in the text's critique)
q: The Jogi runneth about begging for clothes and food

s: Jogis begs for clothes and food (while running about)
q: The Jogi runneth about begging for clothes and food

s: Jogis lacks Guru's instruction (when spiritually ignorant)
q: He who hath not received the Guru's instruction, loseth his honour by his own stupidity.

s: Jogis dwells in peaceful home (when he knows the way)
q: The Jogi who knoweth the way dwelleth in a peaceful home.

s: Jogis wears patched coat (as an external guise)
q: With a patched coat and a bag thou assumest many guises.

s: Jogis wears ashes (hypocritically)
q: Thou hypocritically appliest ashes to thy body, And shalt be punished for thy worldliness by Death's mace.

s: Jogis keeps wives (despite ascetic appearance)
q: Jogis with long hair and ashes on their bodies keep wives.

s: the Word is a highest spiritual discourse
q: Deem the Guru's word the highest of all Utter no other discourse; it were all in vain.

s: the Word removes mourning (when meditated upon)
q: He who meditateth on the Word shall need no mourning.

s: the Word removes pride (through spiritual practice)
q: If pride depart by means of the Word, God's abode shall be attained.

s: the Name provides salvation (when treasured in the heart)
q: God is the primal and infinite Being; by treasuring His name in the heart man shall be saved.

s: the Name assists people (at the Last Hour)
q: Nanak representeth, if Thou give Thy name, it will assist me at the last hour.

s: the Name prevents hell (without God's name)
q: without God's name thou shalt go to hell.

s: mammon causes worldly love (through attachment)
q: Thou lovest mammon and woman, And art neither an anchoret nor a worldly man.

s: mammon causes forgetfulness of Name (through covetousness)
q: Through the covetousness that attacheth to thee thou hast forgotten the Name; thy life hath been wasted in transmigration.

s: world is a place of temporary existence (from which people depart through death)
q: Man entered the world doomed to die; yet he amasseth wealth for long life.

s: transmigration is suffered by he (in superstition)
q: God cannot be obtained unless man enter the Guru's protection; Otherwise he is led astray in superstition and suffereth transmigration.

s: transmigration results from forgetfulness of Name
q: Through the covetousness that attacheth to thee thou hast forgotten the Name; thy life hath been wasted in transmigration.

s: salvation requires virtue
q: All men's accounts shall be taken in God's court And no one shall be saved without good works.

s: salvation requires Guru's instruction
q: Without the Guru's instruction thou shalt not obtain salvation or honour

s: divine knowledge is a good material (for making a spiritual lamp)
q: The knowledge of God is a good material; God will accept a lamp made out of it.

s: virtue form lamp (as its wheel)
q: Make good deeds thy wheel, and mould thy lamp on it; It will accompany thee in this world and the next.

s: meditation provides alms of love (under the Guru's instruction)
q: If the love of God attach to thy heart under the Guru's instruction, Thou shalt easily enjoy the alms of contemplation.

s: God is a primal and infinite Being
q: God is the primal and infinite Being; by treasuring His name in the heart man shall be saved.

s: truth is obtained by practice
q: By the practice of truth, truth is obtained; O false ones, false is your pride.

s: pride causes suffering (through attachment to beauty and wealth)
q: Thou art proud on beholding thy beauty and wealth.

s: pride departs through the Word
q: If pride depart by means of the Word, God's abode shall be attained.

s: sin is punished at Death's gate
q: He who hath not God in his heart and whose conduct is not according to the Word, Shall be bound at Death's gate and punished for his sins.

s: death ends worldly existence (for all people)
q: Man cometh when God sendeth him, and he goeth away when God calleth him.

s: death takes away body (at God's appointed time)
q: He who owneth this body and wealth will take them back

s: Death punishes sin (with Death's mace)
q: Thou hypocritically appliest ashes to thy body, And shalt be punished for thy worldliness by Death's mace.

s: God gives the Name (to those who seek salvation)
q: Nanak representeth, if Thou give Thy name, it will assist me at the last hour.

s: the True Guru's instruction removes pride (through spiritual discipline)
q: Thou hast suffered great pain from the disease of pride; but it shall depart when thou receivest the Guru's instruction.

s: the body is a carriage (drawn by five oxen)
q: The five oxen draw the carriage of the body: The whole goeth well by the contrivance of God.

s: the lamp is made from divine knowledge (and good deeds)
q: The knowledge of God is a good material; God will accept a lamp made out of it. Make good deeds thy wheel, and mould thy lamp on it

s: the lamp provides divine knowledge (when floated on water)
q: Float such a lamp on the water As shall procure thee all knowledge.

s: God judges world (according to people's deeds)
q: All men's accounts shall be taken in God's court And no one shall be saved without good works.

s: Hindus is filled with the Muhammadan creed
q: The Muhammadan creed filleth the ears and hearts of the Hindus.

s: Musalman requires guru or priest (for acceptance)
q: The Musalman may praise himself, But without a guru or a priest he shall not be accepted.

s: the Veds are not obeyed by people (in the degenerate age)
q: Nobody obeyeth the Shastars or the Veds Everybody worshippeth himself.

s: God pardons people
q: God continueth to do what is proper; the Pardoner pardoneth.

s: God owns body
q: He who owneth this body and wealth will take them back; he who feeleth anxiety regarding them shall have sorrow.

s: God grants emancipation (mercifully)
q: Who mercifully granteth emancipation in His court, and pardoneth the sins which man committeth.

s: Guru is a giver and procurer of emancipation (true)
q: The true Guru is the giver and procurer of emancipation.

s: Guru is like lake
q: The Guru is like a lake; we are his beloved swans

s: Guru gives instruction (true)
q: God saveth man through the true Guru's instruction; He blendeth with Himself those who are absorbed in His love.

s: Guru breaks entanglements of pride (true)
q: The true Guru breaketh the entanglements of pride, and hindereth the mind from wandering.

s: Guru protects man (as the Fearless One)
q: The Fearless One, the true Guru is our protector.

s: Nanak repeats the spell of God (in whom the three worlds are contained)
q: Nanak, repeat the spell of God in whom the three worlds are contained.

s: Nanak seeks truth (from God)
q: Nanak, may I obtain the truth! preserve mine honour, O Lord; Thou art the Monarch of monarchs!

s: Sanyasi is a renunciant
q: O Sir, the way of the Sanyasi should be this He should under the Guru's instruction only think of the one God, love His name, and be satisfied with it.

s: Sanyasi serves Guru (true)
q: He who serveth the True Guru and removeth pride from his heart, is a true Sanyasi;

s: Sanyasi is without desire (while in the midst of desires)
q: He who in the midst of desires is without desires, and who loveth the one God is a Sanyasi.

s: Sanyasi subdues passions (with God's name)
q: He chattereth not; he amasseth the wealth of patience and his passions he subdueth with God's name.

s: the pious are not punished by Death
q: Death shall not punish godly people, Nor shall they experience the pain of the difficult road.

s: the pious carry on true dealings (according to God's will)
q: The pious carry on their dealings according to God's will.

s: apostate undergoes transmigration (in eighty-four lakhs of species)
q: The apostate shall undergo the pain of transmigration in eighty-four lakhs of species.

s: apostate does not know the Word
q: How shall the apostate obtain knowledge of the Word? Without a knowledge of the Word man undergoeth transmigration.

s: woman is separated from God
q: She who is separated from God obtaineth no access to Him; how shall she be patient?

s: woman obtains peace (when she has found her Beloved)
q: The wife who hath found her Beloved, the Lord of excellences, sleepeth in peace.

s: woman loves God's love
q: My soul is imbued with the love of the Beloved.

s: the Name causes meeting with God
q: Recognize God's primal love, and worship the great God. Shall Death then, O Nanak, strike thee on the head? Nay; the Name shall cause thee to meet God.

s: the Name provides happiness and final deliverance (through repeating hymns and clasping it to the heart)
q: By repeating hymns containing God's true name and clasping it to the heart, all happiness and final deliverance shall be obtained.

s: the Name saves man
q: No one can be saved without the Name; Nanak, that is the true way to swim across.

s: the Word provides salvation (under the Guru's instruction)
q: Nanak, salvation dependeth upon the instruction of the Guru whom God by perfect good fortune hath caused us to meet.

s: God's love provides emancipation
q: without love for God there is no emancipation.

s: divine knowledge enables beholding God (through the salve of truth)
q: The possessor of divine knowledge applieth the salve of truth to her eyes, and then beholdeth Him who seeth all things.

s: transmigration is the pain (when pride departeth)
q: When pride departeth, doubt, fear, and the pain of transmigration depart.

s: emancipation depends on serving the Guru
q: Salvation dependeth upon serving the Guru, and night and day singing God's praises.

s: Death is a tax-gatherer
q: He whose avarice is extinguished and whose mind is cool, shall owe no tax to Death the tax-gatherer.

s: Death punishes those who repeat not God's praises (at last)
q: They who repeat not God's praises shall be punished at last;

s: God's court is entered by they (with a robe of honour)
q: They shall go with a robe of honour to Thy court and be happy by the True King's order.

s: God is a one God
q: He should under the Guru's instruction only think of the one God, love His name, and be satisfied with it.

s: true merchandise is a God's name
q: Few are they who traffic in true merchandise; they who do so obtain profit. Depart with the merchandise of God's name, And thou shalt easily obtain a sight of God's court.

s: true merchandise provides profit (to those who traffic in it)
q: Few are they who traffic in true merchandise; they who do so obtain profit.

s: world is a terrible ocean
q: This world which is a terrible ocean, is crossed over by the Guru's instruction And by dispelling the heart's doubts.

s: religious life is preserved in home (by drinking God's essence)
q: He who drinketh God's essence and preserveth a religious attitude in his own home shall obtain peace.

s: God has no father, mother, son, or brother
q: He hath not father or mother or son or brother.

s: God is inaccessible and unfathomable
q: God is inaccessible, unfathomable, altogether distinct from His creation.

s: God supports world (carefully)
q: The Creator is the true Lord Who carefully supporteth the globe of the earth.

s: God pervades three worlds
q: Continue to love God, and you shall behold the Unseen One pervading all three worlds.

s: God is known through Guru (by meeting the true Guru and implanting his instruction in the heart)
q: God is known by meeting the true Guru and implanting his instruction in the heart.

s: the Name obtains salvation (for the holy man)
q: Without God's name salvation is not obtained; the holy man obtaineth it by the Name.

s: devotional garb is assumed by man (under the stress of prenatal acts)
q: Yet shall he be not satisfied without God's name; it is under the stress of prenatal acts man assumeth a devotional garb.

s: God is in creatures (in water, dry land, nether regions, and firmament)
q: Thou, O God, art in all creatures that are in the water, the dry land, the nether regions, and the firmament.

s: creatures are in water (all creatures that are in the water)
q: Thou, O God, art in all creatures that are in the water, the dry land, the nether regions, and the firmament.

s: God's elixir is drunk by Nanak (after stirring it)
q: By the favour of the Guru preserve Thy servant; Nanak stirring God's elixir hath drunk it.

s: Nanak drinks God's elixir (after stirring it)
q: By the favour of the Guru preserve Thy servant; Nanak stirring God's elixir hath drunk it.

s: Guru preserves Nanak (by the Guru's favour)
q: By the favour of the Guru preserve Thy servant; Nanak stirring God's elixir hath drunk it.

s: the Name is necessary for salvation
q: Without God's name salvation is not obtained; the holy man obtaineth it by the Name.

s: the Name is necessary for man (for salvation)
q: Without the Guru's instruction, O mortal, where is salvation? without Gods name man is entangled and dieth.

s: man is entangled transmigration (without Gods name)
q: Without the Guru's instruction, O mortal, where is salvation? without Gods name man is entangled and dieth.

s: man dies death (without the Name)
q: To eat poison, to speak for the sake of poison (mammon) without the Name is to die an unprofitable death and wander in transmigration.

s: man wanders in transmigration (after an unprofitable death without the Name)
q: To eat poison, to speak for the sake of poison (mammon) without the Name is to die an unprofitable death and wander in transmigration.

s: the True Guru's instruction is necessary for salvation (for man)
q: Without the Guru's instruction, O mortal, where is salvation? without Gods name man is entangled and dieth.

s: man is saved by the Name (when he repeateth it)
q: Yet shall he not find comfort without God's name; he who repeateth it shall be saved.

s: man assumes devotional garb (under the stress of prenatal acts)
q: Yet shall he be not satisfied without God's name; it is under the stress of prenatal acts man assumeth a devotional garb.

s: virtue has part divine knowledge (as fruit)
q: Good acts are the tree, God's name its branches, religion its flowers, divine knowledge its fruit, Attainment of God its leaves, and the dispelling of mental pride its dense shade.

s: virtue has part attainment of God (as leaves)
q: Good acts are the tree, God's name its branches, religion its flowers, divine knowledge its fruit, Attainment of God its leaves, and the dispelling of mental pride its dense shade.

s: virtue has part mental pride (as dense shade)
q: Good acts are the tree, God's name its branches, religion its flowers, divine knowledge its fruit, Attainment of God its leaves, and the dispelling of mental pride its dense shade.

s: true merchandise is repeated with tongues
q: They who behold God's power with their eyes, hear it with their ears, and repeat the true Name with their tongues, Obtain the full wealth of honour and tranquilly meditate on God.

s: Nanak is a the pious
q: Nanak, the pious who continue absorbed in God shall be perennial and never wither.

s: Nanak is absorbed in God (continually)
q: Nanak, the pious who continue absorbed in God shall be perennial and never wither.

s: Nanak is perennial perennial (while absorbed in God)
q: Nanak, the pious who continue absorbed in God shall be perennial and never wither.

s: spring begins in Rag Basant (ever)
q: All hail to the great month in which spring ever beginneth.

s: God sustains earth
q: Ever and ever remember the Sustainer of the earth, and thy heart shall rejoice.

s: man is a silly man
q: O silly man, forget thy pride, Subdue thy pride and meditate on God in thy heart adopt the most excellent virtues.

s: man should subdue pride
q: O silly man, forget thy pride, Subdue thy pride and meditate on God in thy heart adopt the most excellent virtues.

s: man should adopt virtues (most excellent)
q: O silly man, forget thy pride, Subdue thy pride and meditate on God in thy heart adopt the most excellent virtues.

s: virtue is a tree
q: Good acts are the tree, God's name its branches, religion its flowers, divine knowledge its fruit, Attainment of God its leaves, and the dispelling of mental pride its dense shade.

s: virtue has part the Name (as branches)
q: Good acts are the tree, God's name its branches, religion its flowers, divine knowledge its fruit, Attainment of God its leaves, and the dispelling of mental pride its dense shade.

s: virtue has part religion (as flowers)
q: Good acts are the tree, God's name its branches, religion its flowers, divine knowledge its fruit, Attainment of God its leaves, and the dispelling of mental pride its dense shade.

s: impurity is absent in water
q: There is no impurity in earth, there is no impurity in water;

s: impurity is absent in air
q: There is no impurity contained in air.

s: man without a guru turns away from God
q: It is he who turneth away from God whose mouth is impure.

s: impurity is absent in songs
q: There is no impurity in songs, there is no impurity in knowledge;

s: water generates world
q: Water is the generator of the world, and shall finally destroy everything.

s: water destroys everything (finally)
q: Water is the generator of the world, and shall finally destroy everything.

s: idol is kept in house (with its attendant gods)
q: Thou in thy house keepest an idol with its attendant gods:

s: idol has attendant attendant gods
q: Thou in thy house keepest an idol with its attendant gods:

s: idol receives kungu
q: Thou offerest it kungu, sandal, and flowers

s: idol receives sandal
q: Thou offerest it kungu, sandal, and flowers

s: idol receives flowers
q: Thou offerest it kungu, sandal, and flowers

s: idol does not give sustenance (when hungry)
q: The idol giveth thee not when hungry, nor preserveth thee from death.

s: idol does not preserve from death
q: The idol giveth thee not when hungry, nor preserveth thee from death.

s: God has partner no partner
q: But Thou hast no partner, therefore will I praise Thee to Thy face.

s: impurity is absent in divine knowledge
q: There is no impurity in songs, there is no impurity in knowledge;

s: the Name gives sight to blind
q: Thy name giveth sight to the blind.

s: Kal age has men men (with faces like dogs)
q: In the Kal age men have faces like dogs, and eat carrion.

s: men eats carrion (in the Kal age)
q: In the Kal age men have faces like dogs, and eat carrion.

s: men barks falsehood (as they utter it)
q: They bark as they utter falsehood, and have no regard for honesty.

s: men has regard for honesty (none)
q: They bark as they utter falsehood, and have no regard for honesty.

s: men has honour none (while alive)
q: They who have no honour while alive, shall have an evil reputation after death.

s: men has reputation evil (after death when they lack honour while alive)
q: They who have no honour while alive, shall have an evil reputation after death.

s: destiny takes place what is destined
q: What is destined taketh place, Nanak; what the Creator doeth cometh to pass.

s: impurity is absent in moon (in its different phases)
q: There is no impurity in the moon's or sun's different phases;

s: truth is made fasting (by those foremost in God's favour)
q: They who make truth their fasting, contentment their place of pilgrimage, divine knowledge and meditation their ablutions, Mercy their idol, and forgiveness their rosary, are foremost in God's favour.

s: contentment is made place of pilgrimage (by those foremost in God's favour)
q: They who make truth their fasting, contentment their place of pilgrimage, divine knowledge and meditation their ablutions, Mercy their idol, and forgiveness their rosary, are foremost in God's favour.

s: meditation is made ablutions (by those foremost in God's favour)
q: They who make truth their fasting, contentment their place of pilgrimage, divine knowledge and meditation their ablutions, Mercy their idol, and forgiveness their rosary, are foremost in God's favour.

s: contentment is a place of pilgrimage
q: contentment their place of pilgrimage

s: meditation is a ablutions
q: divine knowledge and meditation their ablutions

s: Mercy is made idol (by those foremost in God's favour)
q: They who make truth their fasting, contentment their place of pilgrimage, divine knowledge and meditation their ablutions, Mercy their idol, and forgiveness their rosary, are foremost in God's favour.

s: right way is made loincloths (by few)
q: Nanak, few there are who make the right way their loincloths, meditation on God their cooking squares, Good deeds their frontal marks, and God's love their food.

s: meditation is made cooking squares (by few, in meditation on God)
q: Nanak, few there are who make the right way their loincloths, meditation on God their cooking squares, Good deeds their frontal marks, and God's love their food.

s: impurity is absent in sun (in its different phases)
q: There is no impurity in the moon's or sun's different phases;

s: virtue is made frontal marks (by few)
q: Nanak, few there are who make the right way their loincloths, meditation on God their cooking squares, Good deeds their frontal marks, and God's love their food.

s: God's love is made food (by few)
q: Nanak, few there are who make the right way their loincloths, meditation on God their cooking squares, Good deeds their frontal marks, and God's love their food.

s: beggar loses caste
q: Another becometh a beggar and loseth his caste.

s: right way is recognized by those who eat the fruit of their labour and bestow something
q: They who eat the fruit of their labour and bestow something, O Nanak, recognize the right way.

s: impurity is absent in corn
q: There is no impurity in corn, there is no impurity in ablution;

s: impurity is absent in ablution
q: There is no impurity in corn, there is no impurity in ablution;

s: impurity is absent in rain (which falleth everywhere)
q: There is no impurity in rain which falleth everywhere

s: impurity is absent in earth
q: There is no impurity in earth, there is no impurity in water;

s: God consults no one (when He destroyeth)
q: He consulteth no one when He createth; He consulteth no one when He destroyeth; He consulteth no one when He giveth or taketh.

s: God gives gifts (countlessly)
q: How great shall the Giver be called who giveth countless gifts!

s: God has full storehouses (in every age)
q: Nanak saith, O God, Thy storehouses are full in every age, and never is there a deficiency.

s: God is immortal deathless
q: He was not born, neither shall He die; True is the Creator.
